newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bourse buoyed by banks and bonds at close.
newsitem.headline: French bourse buoyed by banks and bonds at close.

text.p: French stocks finished sharply up, with a shove from bank stocks after strong first-half results, healthy oil share performance and a tug from rising bonds in the wake of weaker-than-expected U.S. economic inflation data.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 27.31 points or 1.34 percent up at 2,065.37, while the CAC-40 futures contract closed 20 points up from Wednesday at 2066.0.
Volume was a healthy 5.42 billion francs.
Benign U.S. producer price data for August, in terms of prospects for a U.S. interest rate increase, and franc firmness bolstered the bourse, traders said.
Oil and bank stocks buoyed activity, while cyclical stocks also gained on the back of expectations of economic improvement, they said.
Profit-taking could set in on Friday before release of U.S. consumer prices figures, they added.

Banque Nationale de Paris closed 3.0 francs or 1.58 percent higher at 192.5 with a hefty 1.76 million shares traded after the bank beat expectations with an 80 percent first-half rise in net attributable profit to 1.735 billion francs. CCF bank also reported a profit rise.
Analysts judged the first rise in net banking income in two years at BNP as sign of better outlook for bank results in 1996.
Insurer UAP, a key BNP shareholder, firmed on the back of the BNP figures.
Eurotunnel jumped in the afternoon on market talk of a debt deal coming closer, sparked by a report in the British Evening Standard newspaper.
Oil giant and index heavyweight Total firmed, helped by Iraq troubles and positive broker sentiment.
